why: For a fixed peak, the left side is capped by a running minimum, and a monotonic stack finds where the cap changes: best[i] = best[j] + maxHeights[i] * (i - j) where j is the previous smaller cap. Doing this from both sides gives every peak in O(n). It needs the stack plus a DP-on-the-stack insight.
hints: Fix the peak p. What is the best height at each index to its left?
min(maxHeights[j..p]): a running minimum walking away from the peak. The sum of those minimums is what you need for every p.

left[i] = left[j] + maxHeights[i] * (i - j), where j is the previous index with a smaller cap (monotonic stack, pop while cap > maxHeights[i]). Do the same from the right; answer = max(left[i] + right[i] - maxHeights[i]).
pitfalls: The peak is counted in both the left and right sums; subtract it once.
Trying every peak with an O(n) walk is O(n^2), too slow for 10^5.
